title: Every axiom system used in current mathematical research is universal

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Every axiom system used in current mathematical research is universal

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Basic logic and pure predicate logic are not universal, but adding a function or relation with more than one argument gives universality; arithmetic, set theory, group theory and ring theory are universal, and every axiom system actually used in current mathematical research is known to be universal, while heavily constrained systems such as commutative group theory and simplified real algebra and geometry are not.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But of the axiom systems actually used in current mathematics research every single one is now known to be universal.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 12, “The Principle of Computational Equivalence”; section “Implications for Mathematics and Its Foundations” (from p. 772), p. 784. Scope: standard axiom systems of mathematics (logic, predicate logic, arithmetic, set theory, group theory, ring theory, real algebra, geometry)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch12-32: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.56

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The named standard theories can be checked individually through existing proofs. The unrestricted claim about every research axiom system is underspecified and vulnerable to counterexamples, so current resources resolve only its explicit cases.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define universality uniformly as interpretation or simulation of a universal machine, list the named theories precisely, and verify published interpretations or decidability results for each. A non-universal theory actively used in research refutes the universal quantifier.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The broad syntactic claim about adding any multi-argument relation needs qualifications.

"Every axiom system used" has no stable census.

Universality has multiple non-equivalent meanings for theories.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.4
data adequacy: 0.35
discriminating power: 0.75
operationalizability: 0.65
data existence: 0.6

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The named positive and negative cases are classical theorems, and proof libraries contain formalizations of several of them. The sentence also says that every axiom system in actual research use, outside a list of heavily constrained exceptions, is universal. There is no canonical public census of that class, so the theorems settle the examples and leave the quantifier partly checked.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For each named system, use a published proof or decision procedure: propositional logic and pure monadic predicate logic are decidable, arithmetic and set theory interpret computation, the word problem for groups is undecidable, and Tarski's real algebra and elementary geometry are decidable. The clause about every system used in research is scored only relative to an explicit list of fields.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Used in current research is a sociological boundary rather than a formal list.

The exceptions for commutative groups, real algebra, and geometry have to be applied uniformly.

Universality is proved theory by theory, so the universal quantifier needs a census.
